items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta Interview, 1958-07-00
items.q: The interviewee discusses Hamilton Reynolds in response to the interviewer's mention of Hewley, but provides no personal connection or interaction with Hewley himself.

ctx.x: Man, the kick would get out of it, you know. Freshman and all that, you know. I actually like to hear him talk and all that, too. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
Hewley lived up on Plum Street.

At the Hamilton Reynolds house. Oh. I was a nice man, Hamilton Reynolds. He was a great friend of, well, he was a great friend of, he was the head of the board, the number two board of the war, number one world war and all that. Well, he's the, he had, he's the one who got all the streets, he was over all the streets paid. Oh, yeah. Hamilton Reynolds, he was. Big, tall, Jew fellow. There's a nice man, too. Yeah. Oh, that was a lot of years, but years of others. I grew up there at Bar. Oh, it's like Fraternity…
